summary: A business affected by a law has a new decision to make after its repeal.
realLife: When beer sales resumed in 1933, Saul Hoffberger and his partners brought brewing back to Baltimore’s National Brewing Company site. They kept the name and replaced the old brewhouse.
inGame: needs: a played business decision tied to it. lawChain and the dev-law-industries repeal comparison trace a change.
gates: A repeal has taken effect and a business impact is established.

turns.what: The employer keeps the current schedule until its existing contracts expire.
turns.pulledBy: The repeal changes future costs while the signed contracts fix today's terms.
turns.writesBack: The review date falls at contract renewal.

turns.what: A contractor gets the first work at the brewery while the brewing crew waits for the new kettles.
turns.pulledBy: The employer has signed the construction contract and the equipment delivery is still ahead.
turns.writesBack: The town’s employment report dates the construction work and leaves brewery hiring pending.
